title: Asian chip stocks tumble ahead of Nvidia's first post-Huang earnings report
subtitle: TSMC fell 5.7%, SK Hynix 4.3% and Samsung 4.5% on Monday as investors brace for Tuesday's Nvidia Q3 report — the company's first since Jensen Huang's resignation and under interim CEO Colette Kress.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Asian semiconductor stocks sold off sharply on Monday, November 16, ahead of Nvidia's fiscal third-quarter earnings on Tuesday. TSMC closed down 5.7%, SK Hynix fell 4.3%, and Samsung dropped 4.5%, with Taiwan's benchmark off about 6% on the day. In U.S. pre-market trading TSMC was down about 4.24%. Nvidia itself finished Friday down roughly 2% at $162.85, valuing the company at about $4.01 trillion.

This is the first Nvidia report since Jensen Huang's resignation, and the first under Colette Kress, who is serving as both CFO and interim CEO. Investors are watching for three things: whether the Asia data-center route to China holds under the new leadership, whether Rubin and Blackwell Ultra shipment guidance stays on track, and how Nvidia talks about the $250 billion Ohio backstop and other multi-year financing commitments it has underwritten for hyperscalers.

The selloff isn't just about one earnings print. It reflects a deeper nervousness about the AI trade's circular financing: GPUs are collateral for debt that funds the data centers that buy more GPUs. Several of Monday's moves tracked Anthropic's expected Nasdaq debut later in the week as much as Nvidia's report — if the Anthropic listing prices below the $70–$78 roadshow range, investors will read it as a signal that the private-market valuations backing those circular deals have gotten ahead of public-market appetite.

A note for learners: single-company earnings rarely drive 5% moves across Asian chip indexes. When they do, it means the market is pricing a regime question, not a quarterly number. Watch what managers say about cancellation terms, buyer concentration, and inventory — not the revenue beat. The headline number will be the easiest thing to see and the least informative.
